findings.body:
**Write the disable marker before the live configuration.**

`prepare()` writes the rendered configuration at line 646 and the `runner-disabled` marker at line 647. If the process crashes or power is lost between those writes, the new configuration can stay live without the marker. This applies only when no marker existed before preparation. `inactive()` checks only `ActiveState`, so `prepare()` accepts a stopped but enabled timer. `crq-tick.timer` has `WantedBy=timers.target`, so an enabled tick timer can start at the next boot. `tick()` returns early only when the marker exists, so the tick can run on the new configuration without owner approval.

Write the marker first. If a crash occurs after the marker and before the configuration, the host stays inert on its previous configuration.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-        atomic_bytes(root / CONFIG, data)
-        atomic_bytes(root / 'apps/crq-python/state/runner-disabled', b'Prepared inert; owner approval required to start.\n')
+        atomic_bytes(root / 'apps/crq-python/state/runner-disabled', b'Prepared inert; owner approval required to start.\n')
+        atomic_bytes(root / CONFIG, data)
```

</details>
findings.title: Write the disable marker before the live configuration.

findings.body:
**Restore rendered host config if checkout fails.**

`switch()` restores the live host config to the committed bytes before `git checkout --detach target` runs. If the checkout fails, the rendered config stays lost and the retry fails `drift_check`. Keep the rendered bytes and write them back on any failure after the restore.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
         git(root, 'restore', '--', CONFIG)
-        if git(root, 'status', '--porcelain', '--untracked-files=all'):
-            raise ValueError('checkout not clean after config restore')
-        git(root, 'checkout', '--detach', target)
+        try:
+            if git(root, 'status', '--porcelain', '--untracked-files=all'):
+                raise ValueError('checkout not clean after config restore')
+            git(root, 'checkout', '--detach', target)
+        except BaseException:
+            atomic_bytes(root / CONFIG, current)
+            raise
```

</details>
findings.title: Restore rendered host config if checkout fails.

findings.body:
**Make the success output JSON on stdout and narration on stderr.**

`main()` ends with a plain-text `print` to stdout. Doctrine I1 requires each operation invocation to write one JSON artifact to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed. This script's subcommands are dispatched as `args.operation`, so the rule applies to them. No caller in this repository parses this output today, so the impact is a contract breach, not a current caller failure.

<details>
<summary>🐛 Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-    print('completed ' + args.operation + '; no units started')
+    print(json.dumps({'operation': args.operation, 'status': 'ok'}, sort_keys=True))
+    print('completed ' + args.operation + '; no units started', file=sys.stderr)
```

Import `sys` at module scope. `main` imports it locally only when `argv` is `None` (line 741), so `sys` is unbound when `argv` is passed. Shape the JSON to the result contract that the command family uses.

</details>
findings.title: Make the success output JSON on stdout and narration on stderr.
